causal_markov_condition.factorisation_basis: the joint was derived as the product of the validated local CPTs over the DAG, including point-mass CPTs where declared

causal_sufficiency.basis: the fixture's exogenous-noise structure is declared in its authoritative specification; causal sufficiency is not inferred from CPTs or the observational population

ordinary_faithfulness.basis: the exact population CI set equals the graph d-separation set over the exhaustive singleton-pair audit
ordinary_faithfulness.why_singleton_audit_is_sufficient: DAG factorisation establishes the global Markov direction. A DAG d-separates two variable sets exactly when it d-separates every cross-pair, while probabilistic setwise conditional independence implies every cross-pair conditional independence by decomposition. Therefore any extra setwise population independence would yield an extra singleton-pair independence detected by this audit.

cpdag.deterministic_relation_boundary: this is the ordinary graph-theoretic CI-based CPDAG. For fixtures with deterministic variables, functional constraints may change what is identifiable beyond ordinary CI information; no such extended recovery object is asserted here.
cpdag.kind: graph-theoretic essential graph of the generating DAG MEC
cpdag.observational_recovery_scope: this CPDAG is the population-level CI recovery target only under causal sufficiency, the causal Markov condition, and ordinary faithfulness

markov_equivalence_class.method: exact orientation enumeration by skeleton and unshielded colliders

mechanisms.interpretation: all edges active is a local mechanism/minimality check; it is not by itself a faithfulness proof

scope.ci_audit: every unordered singleton variable pair and every subset of the remaining variables
scope.zero_mass_conditioning_assignments: the cross-product identity is vacuously satisfied when P(s)=0; only positive-mass conditioning assignments constrain CI
